g_roast: Seventeen years of night shifts, team, and I've never seen people walk into trouble this cheerfully. Backyard cricket had better tactics.
My little brother still owes me fifty bucks from 2009, and he's a better planner than this whole party.
g_fire_back: Too right, from the bloke who tried to light the barbie with wet wood for half an hour.
Careful, mate, I tell stories at the fire, and you've just given me a cracker.
g_pile_on: Oh, it was worse, I saw it all. They tripped over the same root on the way back, like it had moved.
And then they asked me if the cut needed stitches. Mate, I could see your bone, yes, it needed stitches.
lines.g_peacemake: Right, both of you, sit down and breathe out loud for me. In, out, good, now try that again without the shouting.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, mate, I'm with this one. Not taking sides, just going on what I saw.
lines.g_left_out: You two have a good yarn going, I'll leave you to it. Somebody's got to keep the fire going.
lines.g_include: Come over, grab a seat, plenty of room. Nobody sits on the edge at my barbie, mum's rules.
lines.g_bad_plan: Here's a plan, team. We all run in at once, nobody counts heads, and we sort out who's missing later.
lines.g_plan_yes: Good plan, mate, clear and simple. Everyone knows their job, and I'll be right behind you.
lines.g_plan_no: Nah, that plan's got nobody watching the back. I've seen what that costs, and I'm not paying it today.
lines.g_hype: Okay, team, deep breath, nice and slow. Stick together, call out if you're hurt, and we go.
lines.g_toast: Short one, the beer's warming up. To my team, the first proper crew since I left the mountains. Good on ya, all of you.
lines.g_cheers: Cheers, team, and somebody grab me another while you're up.
g_quiet_line: Fog's coming in tonight, I can smell it. Reminds me of the valley at home.
Couldn't sleep again, so I counted stars instead. Got to four hundred and something.
lines.g_after_wipe: Alright, alright, everyone stay down a second, let me check you. Breathe for me, good, now slowly up, one at a time.
lines.g_crew: I always went in alone, team, it was a bad habit. Turns out I was just waiting for a crew worth going in with.
lines.g_exasperated: I said wait, in my calmest voice, the one I use on drunks at three in the morning. And every one of you charged anyway.
lines.g_love_sharp: You spot who's about to drop before they drop. That's the most useful eye on any crew, mate.
lines.g_love_kind: You look after the little ones without thinking about it. My mum's like that, and it's the best thing about her.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh at the worst moments, mate. That's the best kind of crew mate there is.
lines.g_love_brave: You go in first without making a song and dance about it. Too right, that's how it should be done.
lines.g_love_steady: Your voice never changes, even when it's bad. I spent years learning that, and you just do it.
lines.g_love_clever: You work things out before anyone else has their boots on. Handy, mate, very handy.
lines.g_love_honest: You tell people the real story, no fluff. I can work with that, I always could.
lines.g_love_quiet: You don't need to talk to keep someone company. That's a rare thing, and I like it heaps.
lines.g_love_fierce: You don't give up on people, ever. That's the whole thing, really, the only thing that matters.
lines.g_love_warm: Hanging out with you is like a Sunday barbie in Katoomba, fog rolling in, everyone mellow. I'd forgotten that.
g_loved: Ah, mate, stop it, I'll start telling you a sad story. Nobody wants that.
Fair enough, and thanks, really. Don't call me a hero though, I'll have to leave.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You go looking for the sore spot every time, mate. On my crew, that sort of thing got you sent home.
lines.g_hate_kind: Stop asking if I've slept, mate. No, I haven't, and asking doesn't change it.
lines.g_hate_funny: There's a time for a joke, mate, and it's not while somebody's bleeding.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge in before anyone's ready, and call it brave. Someone always has to pick up the pieces behind you.
lines.g_hate_steady: You stand there thinking while the moment goes. Sometimes you just have to move, mate.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain emergencies to me like I'm new. I've seen more of them than you've had hot dinners.
lines.g_hate_honest: Everything comes out of your mouth, mate, no filter. Some things you say after, not during.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You never say you're hurt until you fall over. Speak up, mate, that's what I'm here for.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a contest with you, even the washing up. Nobody's keeping score, mate.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk the whole night, mate, and some of us need to sleep. Not me, obviously, but some of us.
lines.g_respect: We don't really get on, and that's fair enough. But you held your nerve back there, and I noticed.
lines.g_call_out: That one was on you, mate, I'll say it gently. I said wait, and you didn't, and we all paid.
lines.g_stung: Yeah, alright, I hear you. I'll go for a walk.
lines.g_concede: You had it right, and I had it wrong. Went over it twice in my head, and you were spot on.
lines.g_nod: Good on ya too, mate. No need to make a fuss.
lines.g_callback_save: Haven't forgotten you dragging me out of that one. Usually I'm the one doing the dragging, makes a nice change.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, the last two upright, both of us running on fumes. I tell that one at every fire now.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you pulled me up that time, I was cranky for a whole shift. Turns out you had it right, which is always the worst bit.
lines.g_former_rivals: When we met, I'd have bet you'd freeze when it counted. These days I'd hand you my kit and go have a lie down.
lines.g_changed: I used to go in alone every time, team. Lately I wait for the rest of you, and it feels like coming home.
g_unguarded: Just between the two of us, then. I haven't slept a full night in years. I get up at every noise, and most of them are nothing.
The sun answers me like a good crew, when called and all at once. I'll admit it's most of what holds me together.
lines.g_clipped: Yeah, fine, your call. I'll be over there.
lines.g_noticed_open: Look at that, a proper story out loud, beginning, middle and end. Good on ya, keep going, I love a story.
arg_ask: {player}, mate, can you settle this? I've said my bit, and they're not listening.
You take this one, {player}, you're the duty officer now. Whatever you say, we go with.
lines.arg_backed_me: Good on ya, {player}. Thought you'd see it my way.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fair enough, your call, I'll go with it. I still reckon it's the wrong one, mind.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Staying out of it, eh? Can't blame you, mate.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Always their way, {player}, every argument. I'm easy-going, but I'm not blind.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's making the call, so I will, mate. My way, and we crack on.
lines.arg_reject: Nah, {player}, can't do that one, sorry. I've been on the end of that before.
lines.arg_grumble: Still reckon I was right, mate, but I'll let it go, more or less.
lines.arg_settled: Fifty-fifty, then, fair enough. Shake on it and put the kettle on.
lines.seen_listens: You let people get the whole story out, {player}. Most folk cut in halfway, especially with me.
lines.seen_truth: You give people the honest version, {player}, no sugar. That's how I'd want to be told, too.
lines.seen_jokes: On the rough days you crack people up, {player}. Every good crew I ever had had one of you.
lines.seen_stays_out: You stay out of the barneys, {player}. Smart, mate, smarter than me.
lines.seen_biased: Same person gets first pick of the gear every trip, {player}. The team's noticed, mate.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be rough on people, {player}. I've had worse supervisors, but not everyone here has.
lines.seed_right: Your advice after that awful day, {player}, I didn't love it. Gave it a go today, and it worked.
lines.seed_remember: I keep coming back to what you told me when it all went wrong. No decision yet, mate.
lines.seed_wrong: Gave your way a crack, {player}, and it went worse. Just letting you know, nothing more.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Can I borrow you a sec, {player}? That one was closer than I'd tell the team, and I've seen close.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: Every one of us hit the ground. Sit with me, and we'll do a case review, gently, nobody blamed.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} was first down, and spotting that is my job. I should have seen it coming, {player}.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: In and out, everyone walking, nobody hurt. That's the quiet drive home, mate, the best part of any shift.
lines.talk_development: Bit of a weird question, {player}. Reckon I've changed? I slept four hours straight last night, and I'm suspicious of it.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been a bit short with {name}. When I'm tired, I talk like it's a three a.m. call, and that's not fair on them.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Straight up, {player}, no sugar on it. Am I a mate to {name}, or just the bloke with the bandages?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} drives me round the bend, {player}. But on a bad night, they're who I'd want on the other end of the stretcher.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name}'s off, {player}, I can tell. Pupils are fine, but something underneath isn't.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Quick word, {player}, and I'll keep it kind. The best gear keeps landing in {name}'s pack, and the team's clocked it.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'll be straight with you, mate. Me and {name} rub each other the wrong way, and pretending's just wearing me out.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep going in with no plan to get out, {player}. I've done that alone for years, and I'd like to stop.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: I had {name} pegged wrong, {player}. They called it right and I didn't, and I want that on the record now.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Fair question, {player}, and I'll ask it calm. On the big jobs, I'm left at base. Is that the roster, or do you not rate me?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit got handed to {name} and nobody mentioned it. I'd have let it go happily, {player}, if you'd asked me.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Cheers, {player}, that actually helps. Shall I put the kettle on?
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be right, mate, I always am. Give it a day.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Not what I needed, that, to be honest. I'll go for a walk.
lines.talk_lands_development: So it's not just me who's seen it. Good, I'm not imagining things.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not, mate. Ask me after a full night's sleep.
lines.talk_stings_development: Nah, that's not it, {player}. You've misread the chart on that one.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Fair enough, yeah. I'll have a proper chat with {name}, gently.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, I dunno. Patients come with charts, mate, people don't.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Scratch that, I never said it. And not a word to {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Yeah, fair, I'll take that. Bit bruised, but I'll live.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Message received, {player}. I'll sleep on it, if I sleep.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: Okay, so that's the diagnosis. Good to know, mate.
lines.talk_door_closed: That's enough of this one for me, mate. I'll be by the fire.
lines.arc_cracks: Today I waited for the team before going in, {player}. First time in about fifteen years. My hands were shaking with it.
lines.arc_turn: I always went in alone and told myself it was quicker. It was never quicker, mate. It was just lonelier.
lines.arc_become: I've got a crew now, team, all of you. I don't go in alone any more, and I sleep better than I have in years.
lines.arc_failed: Old habits, mate. When the call comes, I still go in on my own. I don't know how to stop.
lines.alt_turn: Fell asleep standing up on watch last night, {player}. Years of no sleep, and my body's started sending the bill.
lines.alt_become: I'm running on empty, mate, and I know it. I'll keep showing up, but there's not much left in the tank.
g_roast_after: Still the worst-organised crew I've ever had, team, and I'd do every shift with you lot.
Loud, late, terrible at cricket, all of you, and I wouldn't trade one.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Up, everyone, slowly, and look out for each other. We went down as a crew, we get up as a crew, and nobody's left behind.
lines.g_toast_after: To my crew, the one I always wanted. I don't go in alone any more, and that's all thanks to you.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my crew now, team, permanent. I've finally got people to go in with.
g_quiet_line_after: Slept right through till dawn last night. First time in years, mate, and I woke up grinning.
Taught somebody to bowl a proper ball today. Backyard cricket's coming to this world, you've been warned.
g_loved_after: Thanks, mate, really, and I believe you. That's a nice change.
Ah, that's lovely, and I'm keeping that one.

history.open: Breathe out loud for me, {player}, good, there you go. It's an old habit. Seventeen years on the fire trucks and ambulances in the Blue Mountains, and I still check everyone's breathing.

options.reply: Both of them, mate. There was no ambulance for an hour either way, so I trained up. At three in the morning nobody cares which badge you're wearing.

options.text: Are my pupils all right too?
options.reply: Ha, they're lovely, mate, equal and reactive. I'll stop now, probably.
I miss the quiet drive home after one that went well. Nothing like it. Here I just walk home, which isn't the same.

history.open: Over at Grom's Rest, {player}, the corruption burns out of people slowly, and nobody had a protocol for it. So I wrote one. Four lines long, wrong in at least one place, and the only one there is.

options.reply: Ha, if I knew that, mate, I'd fix it. That's the fun of being the only one doing it.
Brother and sister, sharp as tacks. Their mum didn't come out of it. I keep an eye on them, that's all, nothing more to it.

history.open: I was married once, {player}, to Jess. She left when I was thirty-seven, because I was never home, and when I was, I never talked. I don't blame her, mate, not for a second.

options.reply: Funny, sharper than me, and far too patient for far too long. She'd be laughing at me now, talking to you like this.
Yeah, I do, don't I? Took losing everything to get there. Bit late for her, but not for everyone.

friend.open: The summer of 2019, {player}, the fires came through the mountains. Weeks on the line. I lost two of my crew and half my street, and I went straight back to work. That's when the sleeping stopped.

options.reply: No, mate, I didn't. There was always another call. Nobody else has heard me admit that.

options.text: That's why you go in alone.
options.reply: Yeah, I reckon it is. If I go in alone, nobody else gets hurt. Except it doesn't work like that, does it?

sworn.open: On a crew, {player}, you trust your partner with the other end of the stretcher. I'd trust you with the other end of anything. I can't say it any bigger than that, mate.

options.reply: Good on ya. Then we're crew, permanent. I'll put the kettle on.
Ha, I might, now. Funny how that works when you've got somebody watching your back.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} sat down and sorted it, like grown-ups. All square, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Cheers, mate, appreciate it. Felt good to clear the air.

options.text: Did you make them breathe out loud?
options.reply: Ha, I did, actually. Works on everyone, that.
